query: Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys reported to date commonly contain both solid solutions and intermetallic compounds. Induction-melted Al- and Mg-rich alloys reached densities of 2.64–2.75 g/cm3 but all had complex structures; Al20Be20Fe10Si15Ti35 combined a density of 3.91 g/cm3 with 911 HV hardness and oxidation resistance at 700 and 900 °C; compositionally graded MgAlCuZnGd showed region-dependent compression, plasticity, and corrosion behavior; and reported AlMgₓTiSnZn alloys contained a primary BCC constituent together with intermetallic compounds, with x = 1.0 showing the best property combination in that series. Prior studies have emphasized hardness and room-temperature compression, whereas interfacial segregation, interfacial energy, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance remain insufficiently studied. The design must retain a density below 6 g/cm3 and address performance constraints associated with the tendency of Mg and dissimilar constituent elements to form stable intermetallic compounds. Starting from an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state, what single intervention hypothesis could improve its combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance? State the intervention, its proposed causal mechanism, quantitative or directional predictions relative to the as-processed baseline, the composition and operating or test boundaries, the prior experimental evidence supporting the hypothesis, and a controlled experiment with explicit observations that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a controlled amount of refractory elements, such as Hf or Mo, into the Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy can improve its combined mechanical, corrosion, and high-temperature oxidation performance by enhancing the formation of stable precipitates and reducing the tendency to form detrimental intermetallic compounds.
generation.material_initial_state: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state
generation.intervention: Introduction of refractory elements (e.g., Hf or Mo) into the alloy composition
generation.conditions: Alloy processing and testing conditions, including temperature, pressure, and environment
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of stable precipitates and reduction of detrimental intermetallic compounds
generation.mechanism: Enhanced precipitation strengthening and improved corrosion resistance due to the introduction of refractory elements
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved mechanical properties, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation performance
generation.baseline: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy without refractory element addition
generation.boundary: Alloy composition, processing conditions, and testing environment
generation.uncertainty: Optimal amount and type of refractory elements, potential interactions with other alloying elements, and effects on microstructure and properties

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled experiment with varying amounts of refractory elements (e.g., Hf or Mo) added to the Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy, with characterization of microstructure, mechanical properties, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation performance
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of refractory elements does not lead to improved mechanical properties, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation performance, the hypothesis is falsified.
